id: 第四章-终点篇-大导寺信辅的前半生-三-贫穷-p1

en: 第四章-终点篇-大导寺信辅的前半生-三-贫穷
Shinsuke's family could be said to have been quite poor.
u.src: 信辅的家里可以说很是贫穷。

en: But their poverty was not the poverty of the lower classes crowded together in tenement compounds; it was the poverty of the lower middle class, forced to endure even more pain for the sake of outward respectability.
u.src: 但是，他们的贫穷不是杂居在大杂院里的下层阶级的贫穷，而是为了外表体面而不得不忍受更多的痛苦的中下层阶级的贫穷。

en: His father had once been a government official and was now retired,
u.src: 他的父亲从前是官吏，如今已经退休，

en: not counting the small amount of interest from their savings,
u.src: 不包括那一点存款利息在内，

en: the four members of the family plus the maid, five people in all,
u.src: 他们一家四口加上女佣，五个人，

en: had to depend on an annual pension of five hundred yen to make a living.
u.src: 就指望一年五百圆的养老金维持生计。

en: So they had to practice thrift upon thrift.
u.src: 所以，必须节俭又节俭。

en: They lived in a house with a small garden,
u.src: 他们住在一栋有小庭院的屋子里，

en: and even including the entryway, it had only five rooms in all.
u.src: 包括玄关在内总共只有五个房间。

ja: ることができなかった
en: The family members could hardly ever put on a new piece of clothing.
u.src: 家里人几乎很难穿上一件新衣服。

en: Every night his father took his amusement in drinking a cup of cheap liquor, the kind one could not serve openly.
u.src: 父亲每晚总是以喝一杯粗酒——一种拿不到台面上的酒——当做消遣。

en: His mother, too, would put a haori over her kimono to hide the patched sash underneath.
u.src: 母亲也以外面披上和服外褂来掩藏里面布满补丁的腰带。

en: As for Shinsuke, even now he remembered that desk with its smell of paint.
u.src: 而信辅，他直到如今都记得那张带着油漆臭味的书桌。
书桌是中古货，

en: with green velvet pasted over its top,
u.src: 桌面上贴着绿色的绒布，

en: and the drawer pulls shone with a silvery metallic gleam,
u.src: 抽屉的拉把手闪着银色的金属光泽，

en: so at first glance it looked rather handsome.
u.src: 猛一看你还挺漂亮的。

en: In fact, the velvet was very thin,
u.src: 实际上，绒布很薄，

en: and the drawers were also hard to pull open.
u.src: 抽屉也很难拉开。

en: Rather than calling it his desk, it would be better to call it a symbol of his household.
u.src: 与其说这是他的书桌，毋宁说这是他家的象征。

en: It symbolized the more painful life his family lived in order to maintain appearances...
u.src: 象征着他家那种为了顾及体面而过的更加痛苦的生活……

en: Shinsuke felt a deep hatred for this poverty.
u.src: 信辅对这种贫穷有深深的憎恨。

en: No, even now this hatred still remained in his heart and had not faded away.
u.src: 不，直到现在这种憎恨还留在他心里未曾消散。

en: I had no money to buy books, no money to attend summer school, and no money to buy a new overcoat.
u.src: 我没钱买书，没钱参加暑期学校，没钱买新大衣。

en: But his classmates all had these things.
u.src: 但是他的同学们都拥有这一切。

en: He envied them, and at times he even felt jealous of them.
u.src: 他羡慕他们，偶尔还会嫉妒他们。

en: But he would certainly never admit to this envy and jealousy, because he looked down on those incompetent classmates.
u.src: 但是，他肯定不会承认这种羡慕和嫉妒的，因为他瞧不起那些没本事的同学。

en: Still, his hatred of poverty had not changed in the slightest.
u.src: 不过，对于贫穷的这种憎恨，并没有丝毫改变。

en: The old tatami mats, the dim light, the patchy, peeling ivy on the paper doors, everything that represented the shabby poverty of his home filled him with hatred.
u.src: 陈旧的榻榻米、昏暗的灯光、纸门上斑驳脱落的常春藤话貌，这一切代表着家里寒酸的样子都使他感到憎恨。
不过，这还算好的。

en: Because of that shabby life, he even hated his own parents.
u.src: 他甚至因为寒酸的生活，憎恨自己的父母。

en: Especially his bald father, who was even shorter than he was.
u.src: 尤其是那个比他还矮的秃头父亲。

en: His father often came to the school to attend guarantor meetings, and Shinsuke felt ashamed of him when he appeared before his classmates.
u.src: 父亲常常来学校参加保证人会议，信辅对出现在同学面前的父亲感觉羞耻。

en: At the same time, he was ashamed of the inferiority within himself that made him look down on his own father.
u.src: 与此同时，他对于自己瞧不起自己的亲生父亲的这种自卑心里感觉羞耻。

en: Imitating Kunikida Doppo, he wrote a passage called An Account of Not Deceiving Myself, and by now the manuscript paper bearing those words had already yellowed.
u.src: 他模仿国木独步写了一段《不自欺记》，如今写着这段话的稿纸已经泛黄——

en: Can I not love my parents?
u.src: “我不能爱我的父母吗？

en: No, it is not that I cannot love them.
u.src: 不是的，不是不能爱。

en: Although I love my father as a person, I do not love my parents' appearance.
u.src: 我虽然爱父亲的人，但是却不爱父母的样貌。

en: Judging people by their looks is a disgrace for a gentleman.
u.src: 以貌取人，对君子来说是耻辱。

en: How much more so when it is my father's appearance?
u.src: 更何况父亲的外貌呢？

en: And yet, no matter what, I still cannot love my parents' appearance.
u.src: 可是，无论如何，我还是无法爱父母的外貌。”

en: Yet there was something he hated even more than a shabby life: the hypocrisy born of poverty.
u.src: 然而，还有比寒酸的生活更让他憎恨的事，那就是贫穷所致的虚伪。

en: His mother would put cakes in a Fugetsudo box and send them to relatives, but what was inside was not Fugetsudo confectionery at all; it was castella from a nearby sweet shop.
u.src: 母亲用“风月堂”的盒子装蛋糕送亲戚，但是那里面装的根本就不是“风月堂”的和菓子，而是附近点心铺的蜂蜜蛋糕啊！

en: His father was the same, always lecturing everyone on thrift and martial spirit.
u.src: 父亲也是如此，他总是教育大家“勤俭尚武”。

en: But when his father spoke of instruction, there was only one worn old copy of the Yupian; anything beyond that, even a Chinese-Japanese dictionary, counted as luxurious and effeminate.
u.src: 但是，倘若父亲要提到训诫的话，唯有一本陈旧的《玉篇》，除此之外就连《汉和辞典》也算是“奢侈文弱”！

en: Nor was that all: Shinsuke himself knew very well how to lie, and his skill at it was no worse than his parents'.
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，信辅自己也很懂得说谎，而且说谎的本事并不逊于他的父母。

en: His monthly allowance was fifty sen, and if he could get even one sen more, he would spend it on the books and magazines he liked.
u.src: 他每个月的零用钱是五十钱，倘若能够多弄到零花钱，即使只多一分钱，他也会拿去买喜欢的图书和杂志。

en: For that, he would lie and say he had lost his money.
u.src: 他会为此撒谎，说钱弄丢啦！
需要买笔记本啦！

en: He needed to pay class fees.
u.src: 需要缴纳班费啦！

en: In short, he used every excuse he could devise to trick money out of his parents.
u.src: ——总而言之，想方设法用一切借口，骗父母的钱。

en: Even so, there were times when the money was still not enough, and he had to do everything he could to please his parents so he could get next month's allowance early.
u.src: 哪怕是这样，钱还是有不够用的时候，他只能使出浑身解数博得父母的欢心，一遍早点拿到下个月的零花钱。

en: Most of all, he liked to win the favor of his elderly mother, who doted on him.
u.src: 他最喜欢博取宠爱他的老母亲的欢心。

en: Of course, whether he was the one lying or his parents were, none of it was pleasant for him.
u.src: 当然，无论是他自己说谎，还是父母说谎，对他来说不都是愉快的是行情。

en: Nevertheless, he went on lying as before, lying boldly and cunningly.
u.src: 不过，他还是一如既往地说谎，大胆而狡诈的撒谎。

en: For that reason, lying became more important to him than anything else, and from it he could feel a morbid pleasure, a pleasure like having killed something.
u.src: 因此撒谎对他来说，是比什么都特别重要的事，他还能因此感到病态的愉悦——一种好似杀死什么一样的愉悦。

en: In this one respect alone, he was especially like a delinquent boy.
u.src: 唯有在这一点上，他特别像个无良少年。

en: In Notes on Not Deceiving Myself, he once wrote the following passage:
u.src: 他在《不自欺记》里写过这么一段——

en: Doppo says he loves for the sake of love; I say I hate for the sake of hatred.
u.src: “独步说为恋爱而恋爱，我说为憎恨而憎恨。

en: I hate the hatred directed at poverty, the hatred directed at hypocrisy, the hatred directed at everything...
u.src: 憎恨对贫穷的憎恨，憎恨对虚伪的憎恨，憎恨对一切的憎恨……”

en: This was Shinsuke's true feeling: at some point, he had begun to hate his own hatred of poverty.
u.src: 这就是信辅的真心，不知从何时起，他开始憎恨自己对贫穷的憎恨。

en: Until he was twenty, he was constantly tormented by this double hatred.
u.src: 二十岁之前，他一直被这种双重憎恨所困扰。

ja: なかったわけではない。
en: Yet it was not as though he had no happiness at all.
u.src: 然而，他也不是一点幸福都没有。

en: In every examination, his marks were good enough to place him third or fourth.
u.src: 每次考试成绩都能名列第三、第四名。

en: There was also a beautiful boy in a lower grade who showed him kindness of his own accord.
u.src: 还有低年级的美少年，主动对他示好。

en: But these were no more than a little sunlight breaking through a cloudy sky.
u.src: 但是，这些不过是云天里露出的一点阳光罢了。

en: Hatred, heavier than any other feeling, lingered in his heart.
u.src: 憎恨比一切感情都更加沉重的在他心头徘徊。

en: Nor was that all: from some unknown time onward, hatred had left an indelible mark on his heart.
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，不知从何时开始，憎恨在他心里留下了不可磨灭的印记。

en: Even after escaping poverty, he still hated poverty.
u.src: 即使是摆脱贫穷之后，他依然憎恨贫穷。

en: At the same time, he hated luxury just as much as he hated poverty.
u.src: 与此同时，他憎恨奢侈，就像憎恨贫穷一样。

en: His hatred of luxury sprang from the mark left by the poverty of the lower middle class.
u.src: 他对奢侈的憎恨，就源于对中下层阶级贫穷的印记。

en: Or rather, it was the only mark of that lower middle class poverty.
u.src: 亦或是说，是对中下层阶级贫穷的唯一印记。

en: Even now, he could still feel that hatred in his heart.
u.src: 时至今日，他仍然能够感受到心头的那种憎恨。

en: It was the fear of the petty bourgeois middle class, forced to be ready at every moment to fight against poverty...
u.src: 那是不得不时刻准备和贫穷战斗的Petty Bourgeois中产阶级的到的恐惧……

en: That autumn, the year Shinsuke graduated from university, he went to visit a friend who was then studying law.
u.src: 信辅在大学毕业的那年秋天，去探望当时正在读法律系的朋友。

en: They talked in a guest room of about eight tatami mats, where both the walls and the paper sliding doors were very old.
u.src: 他们在一个墙壁和纸门都很陈旧的八张榻榻米大的客室聊天。

en: An old man of about sixty suddenly poked his face out from behind the paper sliding door.
u.src: 一个约莫六十岁的老人偶从纸门后方探出一张脸来。

en: From the old man's face, Shinsuke could tell that he was a retired official who had been drinking heavily for many years.
u.src: 信辅在这个老人的脸上看出，那是一个常年酗酒的退休官吏。
“这位是我的父亲。”

en: His friend briefly introduced the old man.
u.src: 他的朋友简单的介绍了这位老人。

en: The old man did indeed wear an arrogant expression and listened absently to Shinsuke's greeting.
u.src: 老人的确面带傲气，心不在焉的听信辅的问候。

en: Then, before the old man turned to leave, he said to Shinsuke, "Please take your time talking!
u.src: 然后，在老人转身离开之前，他对信辅说：“请慢慢聊吧！
那边有椅子。”

en: In the dim corridor, there were indeed two armchairs set side by side.
u.src: 在昏暗的廊下的确有两张带扶手的椅子并排放着。

en: However, those two chairs had high backs and faded red cushions, and were probably old chairs from about fifty years ago.
u.src: 不过，那两张椅子的椅背很高、红色的软垫已经褪色，大概是五十年前的老旧椅子。

en: In those two chairs, Shinsuke saw the impoverished life of the entire lower middle class.
u.src: 信辅从这两张椅子里看到了整个中下层阶级的贫穷生活。

en: At the same time, he could also see that his friend, like him, felt ashamed to have such a father.
u.src: 与此同时，他也看得出来他的朋友和他一样，为有这样的父亲感觉羞愧。

en: This incident left a deep impression in his memory.
u.src: 这件事情在他记忆里留下了深刻的印象。

en: From then on, these thoughts cast still more confused shadows over his heart.
u.src: 这些思想从此在他心里投下了更多杂乱的阴影。

en: In short, he was indeed the son of a retired government official.
u.src: 总而言之，他的确是一个退休官吏的儿子。

en: Compared with the poverty of the lower class, he had to endure the false poverty of the lower middle class.
u.src: 和下层阶级的贫穷相比，他不得不忍受虚伪的中下层阶级贫穷。
